profile.seoTitle: Surjeet — Full-Stack Fresher & Aspiring Cloud Engineer
profile.seoDescription: Surjeet is a full-stack fresher and BCA student in New Delhi, with an IQSetters internship and five selected projects. Moving toward cloud engineering; currently learning Go and distributed systems.

projects.title: Workforce & Payroll Management Prototype
projects.tagline: Making complex HR processes easier to follow.
projects.summary: A workforce-management prototype with a modular backend and database-backed payroll and employee-loan workflows. Business actions are connected to explicit, persisted states.
projects.problem: Payroll work involves calculations, review, approval and publication. A polished interface cannot replace a clear model of those steps.
highlights: Payroll runs move through draft, calculated, validated, approved and finalized stages.
Finalization publishes payslips through service-layer logic.
Employee-loan workflows validate amounts and tenure, calculate installments and persist approval records.
The modular NestJS application registers JWT, roles and throttling guards.
projects.engineeringFocus: Typed interfaces, service-layer state transitions and persisted business rules.
projects.scopeNote: A prototype, not a production-security or payroll-compliance certification. Tenancy, transactions, calculation rules and test depth require further hardening.

projects.title: Offline-First Personal Finance App
projects.tagline: Everyday money workflows, without relying on a cloud connection.
projects.summary: A mobile finance application with local transaction storage, search, expense splitting and statement reconciliation. Its core logic treats money as structured data, not just a number on a screen.
projects.problem: Transactions become difficult to manage when notes, split amounts and bank statements live in different places. A local-first application keeps those workflows together.
highlights: Relational SQLite storage uses foreign keys, indexes, parameterized queries and FTS5 search.
Expense splits are validated against the transaction total with exact-cent handling.
CSV statement imports feed a reconciliation workflow that generates candidate transaction matches.
Unit-test source covers split rounding, validation, reconciliation and tolerance boundaries.
projects.engineeringFocus: Financial edge cases, local persistence, search and testable domain logic.
projects.scopeNote: Not a cloud banking service or collaborative SaaS. Local PIN/biometric locking is not server authentication. Tests were inspected, not executed during project selection.

projects.title: DiskDoom
projects.tagline: Finding where disk space goes, with controls for how the work gets done.
projects.summary: A native macOS disk-analysis project with staged duplicate detection and a separate licensing backend. It combines filesystem work, resource-aware scanning and a stateful TypeScript service.
projects.problem: A useful disk scanner needs cancellation, exclusions, limits and meaningful partial results. Large directory trees and duplicate files require more than attractive visualizations.
highlights: Cancellable scans include exclusions, scan budgets, cycle detection and partial-result reporting.
Duplicate detection narrows candidates by size, samples content and performs chunked full-file SHA-256 hashing.
Cached hashes can be reused instead of repeating work.
A Cloudflare Durable Object manages activation slots, throttling, deactivation and revocation.
Worker tests cover token validation, tampering and expiry; native scan and safety test sources are also present.
projects.engineeringFocus: Filesystem behavior, staged processing, native development and explicit service state.
projects.scopeNote: No verified macOS release, performance benchmark, cleanup-safety certification or production-user claim. Test sources were reviewed, not executed here.

projects.title: Code Snippet Manager
projects.tagline: The useful bits of code, organized where you work.
projects.summary: A browser-local workspace for creating and finding multi-block code snippets, with persistent organization and combined filters—without a server-backed account system.
projects.problem: Reusable code loses its value when it is hard to find. Snippets need searchable content and clear organization, not just a list of saved text.
highlights: Create snippets containing multiple named code blocks and organize them into workspaces.
Combine text and code search with language, tags, workspaces and favorites filters.
Persist snippets, workspaces and filter preferences in localStorage after hydration.
Favorite or delete entries through the application interface.
projects.engineeringFocus: Reusable hooks, client-side data handling and hydration-aware persistence.
projects.scopeNote: A frontend/localStorage application, not an AI, authentication or cloud-database product. No capacity or speed benchmark is asserted.

projects.title: Local-First Field Service App
projects.tagline: Keeping jobs, time and payment records connected.
projects.summary: A field-service mobile application with persisted job, dispatch, time-entry and invoice-linked payment workflows. Operational details stay connected around each job.
projects.problem: A job involves more than a status label. Assignments, time, activity and payment records need to stay connected as work progresses.
highlights: Persist job assignments, status changes, dispatch records and time entries in SQLite.
Record activity history alongside job transitions.
Track invoice-linked payments and calculate remaining balances.
Use a persisted local work queue with retry and backoff logic.
projects.engineeringFocus: Mobile workflow modeling, linked records and recoverable local task handling.
projects.scopeNote: Local role selection is not server-enforced authentication; payment recording is not payment processing. Cloud sync and production multitenancy are not claimed.

about.heading: Full-stack foundations. A cloud engineering direction.
paragraphs: I’m Surjeet, a full-stack fresher based in New Delhi and currently pursuing a BCA at Shoolini University. I’m building on my internship and application projects as I move toward cloud engineering.

From December 2025 to June 2026, I worked as a full-stack developer intern at IQSetters using NestJS, React and PostgreSQL. I contributed to an HRM platform and built MCP integrations and custom Claude skills for team workflows.
My selected projects explore full-stack workflows, local-first data and developer tools. They reflect application-development experience, with each project’s scope and limitations stated clearly.

I’m currently learning Go and distributed systems. These are learning areas, not professional cloud experience. My next step is a junior full-stack or trainee cloud engineering role where I can contribute and learn from experienced engineers.
I use AI tools to support development, then review, debug and improve the result. Clear interfaces, explicit data flows and checking assumptions remain central to how I work.

experience.summary: Hands-on full-stack development with React, NestJS, and PostgreSQL, supported by AI-assisted workflows.
bullets: Contributed to an HRM platform, connecting React interfaces with NestJS services and PostgreSQL data.
Built custom MCP servers and Claude skills for team-specific development tasks.
Matched open-source and frontier models to task complexity to manage API costs and support iteration.
